entries.name: let
entries.description: Create an immutable lexical binding.
entries.parameters: `name` must be a valid identifier; `expression` is evaluated once before binding.
entries.returns: No standalone value; the binding is available in the remaining lexical scope.
details: A later assignment to the same binding is rejected. Inner scopes may deliberately shadow an outer binding.
entries.example:
let answer = 42
emit answer
# 42u64

entries.name: let?
entries.description: Extract a successful `Result` or present `Option` into an immutable binding.
entries.parameters: The expression must evaluate to `Result` or `Option`.
entries.returns: No standalone value; the binding is available to the remaining block or scope.
details: `Result` metadata and causes remain intact. Native C lowers successful `Result` extraction for its parity-tested subset; failed results and options outside that subset remain explicit native boundaries.
entries.errors: A non-`Result`/non-`Option` operand is an argument error; an absent or failed container propagates its structured error.
entries.example:
let? value = ok(41)
emit value + 1 # 42

entries.name: func
entries.description: Declare a lexical function with optional checked parameter and return types.
entries.parameters: Each parameter is an immutable local binding. Write its canonical type after its name with no colon. Callback types use forms such as `func(u32) string`.
entries.returns: An annotated result checks every reachable `return`, tail expression, and fallthrough path before execution. An omitted result remains dynamic for compatibility.
entries.returnValue: `func double(value u32) u32 => value * u32(2)` has type `func(u32) u32`; `double(u32(21))` returns `42u32`.
details: Functions may capture lexical bindings. Signatures are declared before bodies are checked, so recursion and mutual recursion do not require execution.
Known argument and result mismatches are source-located `type_error` diagnostics. A dynamic value crossing a typed boundary keeps a runtime guard.
Function signatures are exact: `func(u32) string` is different from `func(u64) string`. Use the broad `function` kind only when any callable is intended.
Supported native programs lower direct functions and proven closures with exact signature metadata; unsupported runtime-kind assertions fail native compilation clearly.
entries.errors: Unknown type names, wrong arity, incompatible arguments, inconsistent returns, and a non-`null` function that can fall through are errors.

entries.name: emit
entries.description: Append one value to the program's ordered output and continue execution.
entries.parameters: Each expression is evaluated once in source order. Multiple expressions are concatenated into one value with `, ` separators.
entries.returns: No block value. `emit` is a statement and does not replace a tail expression or `return`.
entries.returnValue: The rendered value is committed at that execution point. Earlier emissions remain visible if later work fails or is cancelled.
details: `emit` is valid at the top level and in synchronously executed loops, functions, closures, ordinary blocks, selected call-shaped `if` branches, `match`/`switch` arms, `try`/`catch` bodies, and expanded macro blocks.
Module initialization cannot emit, but a synchronously called exported function may emit into the caller's sequence.

Concurrent `spawn`, `parallel`, `race`, `select`, and `timeout` bodies cannot emit directly or through a called function. Return a value and emit it from the synchronous caller after `await` where applicable.
entries.errors: Concurrent execution reports a structured error at the direct `emit` or statically known emitting call. Module initialization reports a source-spanned error.

entries.name: var
entries.description: Create a mutable local cell and replace its value explicitly.
entries.parameters: The declaration initializer is evaluated before the cell is installed. An assignment target must be a mutable local; `let` bindings, parameters, imports, struct fields, and collection indexes are not assignable.
entries.returns: No standalone value. Assignment commits only after its right-hand side succeeds.
entries.returnValue: `var total = 0` installs `total`; `total = total + 2` commits `2u64` to that cell.
details: Values remain copy-on-write and aggregate updates remain value-semantic. A closure observes later writes to its captured cell, while a spawned task receives a value snapshot and cannot write the parent task's cell.
Assignments are ordered barriers. Errors and cancellation leave the previous value unchanged; use `with`, `setat`, and other value-returning builders for aggregate updates.
entries.errors: Undefined or immutable targets, unsupported field/index targets, failed right-hand sides, and cancellation are errors.
entries.example:
var total = 0
total = total + 2
emit total
# 2u64

entries.name: to_option
entries.description: Convert a `Result` into an `Option` without discarding success payloads.
entries.parameters: One `Result`.
entries.returns: `Option`.
details: The error payload is intentionally not carried into `Option`. Use `Result` when the failure reason must remain observable.
entries.errors: A non-`Result` argument is an error.
entries.example:
emit to_option(ok(11))
# some(11)

entries.name: to_result
entries.description: Convert an `Option` into a `Result`.
entries.parameters: One `Option` and an optional message used when it is empty.
entries.returns: `Result`.
details: An empty `Option` becomes a structured `not_found` error. A supplied message changes that error message, not its stable kind.
entries.errors: A non-`Option` argument is an error.
entries.example:
emit to_result(some(12))
# ok(12)

entries.name: collect
entries.description: Collect successful `Result` or `Option` items into one `Result` containing a `list`.
entries.parameters: One `list` whose items are `Result` or `Option` values.
entries.returns: `Result<List>`.
details: Evaluation stops at the first failure or absent `Option`. A failed `Result` retains its kind, message, metadata, and cause.
entries.errors: An empty `Option` becomes `not_found`; a non-container item is an argument error.
entries.example:
emit collect([ok(1), some(2), ok(3)])
# ok([1, 2, 3])

entries.name: discard
entries.description: Mark deliberate non-handling of a fallible value.
entries.parameters: Exactly one `Result`, `Option`, or structured error.
entries.returns: `null`.
details: `discard` does not unwrap, rewrite, log, or inspect the supplied payload.
entries.errors: An ordinary value is rejected so `discard` cannot hide arbitrary expressions.
entries.example:
discard(err(error(InvalidArgument, "optional telemetry")))
# null

entries.name: must_handle
entries.description: Mark a `Result` as carrying an explicit fallibility contract.
entries.parameters: One `Result`.
entries.returns: The same logical `Result` with immutable metadata.
details: `Result`-preserving combinators retain the marker. `discard` is the explicit intentional-consumption boundary.
entries.errors: A non-`Result` argument is an error. Native C lowering does not yet support `Result` operations.
entries.example:
emit is_must_handle(must_handle(ok(1)))
# true

entries.name: is_must_handle
entries.description: Inspect a `Result`’s must-handle marker.
entries.parameters: One `Result`.
entries.returns: `bool`.
details: The marker is metadata rather than a wrapper, so the underlying `Result` payload and error contract are unchanged.
entries.errors: A non-`Result` argument is an error.
entries.example:
emit is_must_handle(ok(1))
# false

entries.name: try/catch
entries.description: Handle a structured failure as an expression.
entries.parameters: The `catch` binding receives the structured error when the `try` expression fails.
entries.returns: The successful `try` value or the `catch` expression value.
entries.returnValue: A missing file can produce `err.kind` equal to `"not_found"`.
details: Portable kinds include `cancelled`, `timeout`, `not_found`, `permission_denied`, `already_exists`, `io_error`, `invalid_argument`, `unavailable`, `network_error`, and `out_of_range` for `EOF`.
entries.example:
emit try { read("/definitely/missing.osiris") } catch err { err.kind }
# "not_found"

entries.name: redact
entries.description: Remove sensitive details before a structured error crosses a trust boundary.
entries.parameters: One structured error; `Result` and `Option` containers are not accepted directly.
entries.returns: A structured error with safe public fields.
entries.returnValue: `redact` removes stack/debug details and conventional secret-bearing metadata recursively through causes.
details: Public kind and safe public fields remain available for programmatic handling. Native `errno` data is debug-only and never a portable message contract.
entries.errors: A non-error argument is an error.

entries.name: typed let
entries.description: Bind a value while requiring one canonical runtime type.
entries.parameters: `Type` is a canonical scalar or runtime kind, or an exact function type such as `func(u32) string`.
entries.returns: The declaration emits no value.
entries.returnValue: An unsuffixed non-negative integer literal may be checked and fitted to an annotated integer width.
details: Annotations are checked constraints, never implicit casts. `let size u32 = 3` is valid; `let size u32 = 3u64` and `let size u32 = anotherU64` are errors. Use `u32(value)` for an explicit conversion. Bare `let size = 3` continues to infer `u64`.
entries.errors: Unknown annotations, incompatible values, and out-of-range inferred integer literals are errors.
entries.example:
let total u32 = 3
let label string = "ready"
emit total, label
# 3u32
# "ready"

entries.name: if
entries.description: Select one expression from a boolean condition.
entries.parameters: `condition` is evaluated first; `then` and `else` are the two branch expressions.
entries.returns: The selected branch value.
details: Only the selected branch is evaluated.
entries.example:
emit if(true, "yes", "no")
# "yes"

entries.name: match
entries.description: Evaluate a subject once and select the first matching pattern arm.
entries.parameters: Patterns may be literals, wildcards, bindings, lists, or qualified `enum` cases.
entries.returns: The selected arm value.
details: Use `_` or `default` for a catch-all. `Enum` matches without one are checked for missing cases.
entries.errors: Dynamic unmatched values and invalid, unreachable, or non-exhaustive `enum` arms are errors.

entries.name: switch
entries.description: Use `match` semantics with `switch`-oriented branch-table spelling.
entries.parameters: The subject and patterns follow the `match` contract.
entries.returns: The selected arm value.
details: `switch` evaluates its subject once and does not alter pattern or return semantics.
entries.errors: It has the same unmatched-value and exhaustiveness errors for `enum` arms as `match`.
entries.example:
emit switch 0 { 0 => "zero", _ => "other" }
# "zero"

entries.name: enum
entries.description: Declare a closed nominal enumeration.
entries.parameters: Each case has zero or more declared payload fields.
entries.returns: The declaration itself emits no value; cases are values or checked constructors.
entries.returnValue: `Name.Case` evaluates to a zero-payload `enum` value; `Name.PayloadCase(1)` constructs a payload case.
details: `Enum` equality compares declared `enum`, case, and payload without primitive coercion. A backed declaration uses explicit unique `string` or fixed-width integer literals, remains nominal, and never implicitly converts to its backing primitive. JSON serialization keeps that identity as `{"enum": {"type": "Name", "case": "Case", "payload": [...]}}`; this is serialization, not a cast to the backing value. Native C lowers nominal unit and payload `enum` construction, recursive equality/rendering, truthiness, and `match` dispatch for nested `enum`/`list` payloads, literal, type, relational, logical, grouped, guarded, and repeated-binding patterns through its tagged `ABI`.
entries.errors: Empty or duplicate declarations and invalid constructor arity are source-located errors.

entries.name: guarded match
entries.signature: match subject { Pattern when condition => value, default => value }
entries.description: Refine a matching pattern with a condition evaluated only after that pattern succeeds.
entries.parameters: A guard may use bindings introduced by its preceding pattern. `default` must be final and cannot be guarded.
entries.returns: The first arm whose pattern and guard both succeed.
entries.returnValue: A `false` guard falls through to later arms.
details: Grouped alternatives use `|` and must bind exactly the same names. Relational, type, logical, and negated patterns follow the language pattern contract.
entries.errors: Invalid grouped bindings, a guarded `default`, and an unreachable arm are errors.

entries.name: struct
entries.description: Declare an immutable, ordered product type with named fields and optional Go-style metadata tags.
entries.parameters: Each field has a unique name and canonical type. Tags are space-separated `namespace:"value"` pairs; the `json` namespace controls JSON names and `omitempty`.
entries.returns: A nominal struct type and its positional constructor.
entries.returnValue: `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }` constructs a `Point` value; `point.x` reads a field.
details: Fields retain declaration order, tags, and their declared types. Struct equality requires the same nominal type and equal fields. Values are immutable; use `with` for a copied update.

Unknown tag namespaces are preserved for codecs and tooling. Duplicate namespaces, malformed quoting, duplicate fields, missing fields, and unknown initializer fields are rejected with source locations.
A struct may name a previously declared or self-referential struct field type. Values remain finite immutable trees: construction cannot create an implicit cycle or mutable back-reference.
entries.errors: Invalid tags, duplicate or missing fields, wrong constructor arity, and field access on a non-struct are errors.

entries.name: tuple
entries.description: Construct an ordered heterogeneous tuple.
entries.parameters: Tuple items may have different types and are evaluated from left to right.
entries.returns: A tuple value indexed with `[index]` or destructured in a `let` binding.
details: Tuple equality is ordered and structural. `let (name, count) = value` binds each item immutably; the number of names must match the tuple length.
entries.errors: Non-integer or out-of-range indexes and destructuring a non-tuple are errors.
entries.example:
let pair = ("ready", u64(3))
let (state, count) = pair
emit state, count
# "ready", 3u64

entries.name: type
entries.description: Declare an identity-preserving alias for an existing type.
entries.parameters: The target must be a known canonical or previously declared type.
entries.returns: An alias constructor with the target type's runtime identity and conversion rules.
details: Aliases do not create a new nominal runtime kind. They are useful for naming domain concepts while retaining ordinary assignment and arithmetic compatibility.
entries.errors: Unknown targets and incompatible uses are errors.
entries.example:
type Count = u64
let count = Count(3)
emit count
# 3u64

entries.name: newtype
entries.description: Declare a nominal wrapper that requires explicit construction and preserves its own runtime identity.
entries.parameters: One existing type. Construct with `Name(value)` and access the wrapped value through `.value`.
entries.returns: A distinct nominal type; it does not implicitly coerce to its target type.
details: Newtypes compare only with the same nominal type, serialize their declared fields, and require explicit conversion at typed boundaries.
entries.errors: Implicit assignment to the target type, wrong constructor arity, and invalid target types are errors.
entries.example:
newtype UserID u64
let id = UserID(u64(7))
emit id.value
# 7u64

entries.name: with
entries.description: Create an immutable copy of a struct with selected fields replaced.
entries.parameters: The base must be a struct value; each update field must be declared by that struct.
entries.returns: A new value of the same nominal struct type.
entries.returnValue: `point with { x: u64(3) }` leaves `point` unchanged and returns a copy with `x` set to `3u64`.
details: Updates preserve declaration order, field tags, and nominal identity. Missing fields retain their original values.
entries.errors: Updating an unknown field or a non-struct value is an error.

entries.name: trait
entries.description: Declare a nominal behavioral contract. `interface` is an accepted spelling with the same semantics.
entries.parameters: Each method signature names its ordinary parameters and optional return type. A type conforms only through an explicit `impl Trait for Type` declaration.
entries.returns: A statically checked trait boundary.
entries.returnValue: A value assigned to a trait type retains its underlying runtime value and dispatches declared methods through the nominal implementation.
details: Duplicate methods, missing implementations, duplicate implementations, and signature conflicts are deterministic source-spanned checker errors.

Trait and interface values use the underlying runtime value; equality does not compare witness identity. Native C uses a tagged witness table for supported primitive receivers and rejects captured or product-type receiver layouts at compile time.
A receiver method may be declared as `func (value Type) method(...) ReturnType => expression` or in the short form inside an `impl` block.

entries.name: for-iteration
entries.description: Consume the shared lazy iteration contract with cancellation-aware resource boundaries.
entries.parameters: Lists, tuples, Unicode strings, tensors, maps, sets, and readable streams are supported. Maps yield ordered keys and streams yield lines until EOF.
entries.returns: No standalone value; the loop item is scoped to the body.
entries.returnValue: The loop body observes each item in iteration order; an empty iterable executes zero times. Finite collections are not copied and streams are read one item at a time.
details: Existing list order and loop control behavior remain compatible. Unsupported values produce a runtime type error.
Stream iteration observes the current context before each read and stops only at EOF or cancellation. User structs may provide iter() and a next() method returning some(value) or none().
